Let  
\[
A_n=n^3+4,\qquad B_n=(n+1)^3+4.
\]
Then
\[
B_n-A_n=(n+1)^3+4-(n^3+4)=3n^2+3n+1.
\]
Since \(d_n=\gcd(A_n,B_n)\), we have
\[
d_n\mid A_n,\qquad d_n\mid B_n-A_n=3n^2+3n+1.
\]

Now compute
\[
3A_n-n(B_n-A_n)=3(n^3+4)-n(3n^2+3n+1)
=-3n^2-n+12.
\]
Thus
\[
d_n\mid 3n^2+n-12.
\]

Subtracting,
\[
(3n^2+3n+1)-(3n^2+n-12)=2n+13,
\]
so
\[
d_n\mid 2n+13.
\]

Now use the identity
\[
433=4(3n^2+n-12)+76(2n+13)-3(2n+13)^2.
\]
Since \(d_n\mid 3n^2+n-12\) and \(d_n\mid 2n+13\), it follows that
\[
d_n\mid 433
\]
for every positive integer \(n\). Hence
\[
d_n\le 433.
\]

It remains to check that \(433\) is actually attained. Take \(n=210\). Then
\[
210^3+4=9\,261\,004=433\cdot 21388,
\]
and
\[
211^3+4=9\,393\,935=433\cdot 21695.
\]
Therefore
\[
433\mid d_{210}.
\]
But we already know \(d_{210}\mid 433\), so
\[
d_{210}=433.
\]

Thus the maximum value of \(d_n\) is

\[
\boxed{433}
\]
